title: The Great Recall
summary: The state that inherited Tessell's coloniser has returned with a list of machines it says were never abandoned.
body: The Aurelian Compact came to Tessell to strip it. When its charter lapsed, it shipped what it could and left inside a year. Nearly a century later the Aurelian Continuance arrived in person, carrying the Compact's seals, its debt ledgers and a civil bureau called the Recall Authority.

The return began with a Tessellan root collar exported as scrap. It answered a Continuance service reader, proving the old inventory had survived, and an archive audit recovered the Compact's root manifest. Authorization, tender fitting and transit took years. The General Reversion Order reached Tessell when the ships did.

The General Reversion Order does not claim Tessell. It claims the walker roots the Compact left on it: serialized reactor cradles, structural keels and control lattices that every surviving mech still carries beneath its repairs. The Authority calls them inherited state property. Tessell calls them the machines that kept its towns alive after the owner walked away.

The expedition is a repossession tender with a finite guard, not an invasion fleet. It came expecting inspections, surrenders and local compliance. The recovered roots are meant to keep failing reserve and civil-defence walkers around Continuance settlements operational, not merely to settle an old ledger. Every root the guard cores is property it cannot replace; every root it takes intact makes the next seizure easier.

A service reader can ask a dormant root for its serial and maintenance record. It cannot start the reactor, steer the legs, move a gun or tell the Authority where the machine is. The Continuance brought proof of identity, not a buried hand on the controls. Ownership remains paperwork until somebody comes with a tow rig or weapons.
